column7: Decides whether a backend is hidden from the caller, so a call naming it is refused exactly as an unregistered name: unlisted for this caller and not kept by the caller's own per-user slot

Decides whether the listing leaves a backend out for this caller: no policy hides nothing, a grant refusal stays the grant's answer, a cold catalogue hides only a backend refused by name, agent auth with no agent admits none, a truncated catalogue proves no refusal

Decides whether the caller's own per-user slot keeps a backend visible: a held slot that admits a tool keeps it, a cold, stale or truncated slot proves no refusal and keeps it, the shared listing otherwise stands
Decides from the backend name alone whether every tool on it is refused: an mTLS rule denying it or leaving it out of its allow list, or agent scopes granting nothing on it
Decides whether some tool on a backend passes the caller's agent scopes and mTLS policy; shared by the backend admission check and the hiding judgment
Whether a cold backend's name is registered (a backend or the capability provider), read from the registry directly; a mistake would hide an unregistered name's twin or none
Builds the caller's hiding judgment from its authorizer, proven identity and session; a wrong identity would judge hiding as another caller
Hands the hiding judgment the caller's client, agent identity and certificate; a swapped or dropped identity would judge with the wrong caller
Installs a task run's caller so its lookups judge hiding live as that caller; a missed install would hide nothing for the run
Carries what the caller proved at submit to the run's hiding judgment, which picks the caller's own per-user slot from it

Decides which session a direct request runs under: the presented session only when the caller owns it, by the /mcp owner rule, so the call is judged and routed under that session's routing profile and never under another caller's
Installs the direct route's caller, under its owned session, as the request's hiding judgment before the scoped view is read; a wrong identity or session would judge hiding as another caller
